To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“StrateFy, a globally calibrated ordi- nation method using leaf area, SLA and LDMC, worked surprisingly well in an experimentally manipulated grassland community, but failed to predict a significant decrease in CCWM as stress or disturbance increased.”

“StrateFy, using only three easily-measured leaf traits, can predict the functional signature along experimentally manipulated stress and disturbance gradients in herbaceous vegetation, with the exception of the C-dimension”.
CSR theory can predict the functional signature along experimentally manipulated resource gradients, but not disturbance gradients, in herbaceous plant communities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of CSR theory in an experimental context.
the question of whether CSR theory can explain the functional composition of plant communities along experimentally manipulated environmental gradients.

a fundamental question of community ecology: can CSR theory, in combination with a simple, globally calibrated ordination, predict the functional signature and trait evolution of herbaceous vegetation across gradients of soil resources and density-independent mortality?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the predictions of CSR are supported by our data, but only when the traits of the focal species are considered in a global context.
CSR theory was only partially supported by our study, but StrateFy was a useful ordination method.

CSR ordination is an important tool for predicting vegetation response along gradients of soil fertility (stress) and disturbance, but the predictions for the C-dimensions of the triangle are not robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CSR theory was not strongly supported by our experimental study, but the CSR ordination method, in conjunction with leaf traits, did a good job of predicting the functional signature of the vegetation.
StrateFy is a promising new tool for the functional ecologist.
StrateFy is useful for detecting the CSR signature of a community and for testing the predictions of CSR in experimental studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSR theory, when combined with a globally calibrated ordinations, can be a powerful tool to predict functional trait responses to environmental gradients.
the CSR theory is not a universal theory, and that the relative importance of its three dimensions may differ between different plant communities.
CSR theory, in the context of StrateFy ordination, can explain the functional composition of herbaceous vegetation under experimental manipulation of resource availability and disturbance.
